prediction.likelyOutcome: The landlord should recover essentially all of the accrued, pre-surrender rent and additional rent (the strongest, best-documented components), plus small fee/electric items, but the $2,500,000 security-deposit 'replenishment' claim is likely to be substantially discounted or rejected absent proof of an actual replenishment covenant and a prior draw-down, and any post-surrender 'ongoing rent' theory will be tempered by the landlord's total lack of shown mitigation/reletting effort. Net recovery is likely to land well under the complaint's full $3,238,504.15 ask, closer to the undisputed rent components plus only a partial recovery on the deposit theory.

outcome.description: After a non-jury trial the court entered judgment for the landlord for $223,000, the rent due through July 1, 2022 when it regained possession, holding the tenant had been evicted (not abandoned) so the landlord could not recover post-possession rent; it denied the landlord's post-trial claim to $2,149,435.75 in actual damages. The Superior Court affirmed.
